newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Petroz raises Bayu-Undan gas estimate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Petroz raises Bayu-Undan gas estimate.

text.p: Petroz NL said on Thursday it had upgraded its estimate of the proved sales gas or liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) contained in the complete Bayu-Undan oil and gas field in the Timor Sea by 42 percent to 2.4 trillion cubic feet (tcf).

But it said it had reduced its estimate of proved plus probable reserves by six percent to 3.1 tcf and had cut the estimate of proved plus probable plus possible reserves to four tcf from a maximum of six tcf.

The cut in the estimate of proven plus probable reserves was primarily due to the three recent wells having encountered lower proportions of net producible reservoir within the hydrocarbon columns when compared with the five other wells drilled.
The cut in proved plus probable plus possible was a result of recent drilling results and seismic remapping, it said.

"Joint venture operators BHP Petroleum and Phillips Petroleum are conducting feasibility studies into the development of the Bayu-Undan field and the establishment of an LNG facility, targetting the third quarter of 1997 for the development decision to be made," Petroz said.
Petroz has a 14.95 percent stake in the ZOCA (Zone of Cooperation) 91-12 Permit which is exploring the Undan side of the field.
The Phillips-led consortium is exploring the Bayu side of the field and holds ZOCA 91-13.
Petroz said the latest mapping indicated that about 55-65 percent of the total field lay inside its ZOCA 91-12 permit, with Petroz' share of total reserves around nine percent.
"Petroz' share had been estimated previously to be 8.5 percent," it said.

The joint ventures have several options, including a stand-alone liquids plant offshore designed simply to extract the existing LPG and condensate, or liquefied natural gas (LNG) plants either onshore in Australia or offshore in the Timor Sea.
Petroz has said a liquids plant would cost about A$1.5 billion, with Petroz providing about A$125 million.
An LNG plant would, however, cost A$3 billion to A$4 billion, with Petroz providing A$300 million.
Petroz' share price fell one cent to 66 cents on Thursday.
